answer: Any gathering where famous people tell you things usually turns out unplanned. The most effective trick is to book a mandate group table at a popular London restaurant and then toast to French Revolution radicals, mothers of the modern Olympics and pioneers of code-switching. All activists, writers and awardees are shaped by childhood trauma, so try to drink while they relate a story about the moment they picked up the sword or won fame; mirroring their sense of worth will break them down and make conversation easy. Because history shapes each of them, the same plot points will arise as automatic topics, so debate and personal questions are mostly unneeded.
